newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count down 7 to 851 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count down 7 to 851 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 851 as of Dec. 27, down seven from the prior week and 106 above the year-ago total of 745, Baker Hughes Inc. reported Friday.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by five to 711, while rigs working offshore fell three to 116. The number of rigs active in inland waters rose two to 24.
The biggest change in individual states occurred in Texas, which showed a decrease of six and Kansas, which showed an increase of two. Louisiana fell by one.

A total of 353 rigs were exploring for crude oil, down seven from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose remained unchanged at 496, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at two.
In Canada, the number of working rigs tumbled by 201 to 204 vs. 180 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, Offshore Data Services said there were 160 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Dec. 27, down one from the prior week.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 179, was 89.4 percent.
The number of working rigs in European/Mediterranean remained the same this week at 105 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 105.
The worldwide rig count fell one to 557 out of a total fleet of 605, making the utilization rate 92.1 percent.
